s: Which one of the following correctly describes the broad distribution of residual and drifted soils in India?
o: Drifted soils dominate the Deccan Plateau, while residual soils dominate the Indo-Gangetic Plain
Residual soils dominate Peninsular India, while drifted soils dominate North India
Residual soils dominate North India, while drifted soils dominate Peninsular India
Both residual and drifted soils are confined mainly to the coastal plains
x: Residual or in situ soils dominate Peninsular India, whereas drifted or ex situ soils dominate North India.
tq: Use the broad regional comparison to eliminate the reversed distribution.

s: How many major soil types are generally recognised in the classification presented for India?
x: The classification recognises eight major soil types: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.
tq: Directly recall the number attached to the classification.

2. It is particularly associated with the Indo-Gangetic Plain, deltas and coastal areas.
3. It is generally suitable for irrigated farming.

x: Alluvial soil is the most widespread soil, covers the Indo-Gangetic Plain, deltas and coasts, and is well suited to irrigated farming.

Bhabar — belt of pebbly alluvial fans
Terai — dry upland above the flood plain

River deposits in the Indo-Gangetic Plain

s: Which one of the following is a characteristic of red and yellow soil?

Black colour and neutral to alkaline reaction
Very high moisture retention and abundance of humus
Porous and light texture with low moisture retention
x: Red and yellow soils are generally porous and light, with low moisture retention. They are also poor in lime, humus and phosphoric acid.
tq: Contrast the physical and nutrient properties with those of black soil.

s: Laterite soil is formed under which combination of conditions?
o: Waterlogging and accumulation of organic matter in humid lowlands
Low rainfall and low temperature with deposition of salts
Heavy leaching, rainfall above 200 cm and high temperature
x: Laterite forms through intense leaching under heavy rainfall exceeding 200 cm and high temperature.
tq: Identify the soil from the environmental process rather than from its location.

s: Which one of the following statements about laterite soil is correct?
o: It is generally fertile without manuring and is rich in nitrogen and phosphate
It is rich in iron and aluminium oxides and is generally acidic and infertile
It is formed mainly from river deposits and contains abundant kankar
It has the highest moisture retention among Indian soils
x: Laterite soil is rich in iron and aluminium oxides but is generally acidic and infertile. It is poor in nitrogen, phosphate and calcium and has excess iron oxide and potash.
tq: Watch for the nutrient reversal trap in statements about laterite.

s:

Saline soil — upper Himalayan slopes above the tree line
Peaty soil — western Rajasthan and the Thar
Arid soil — Sundarbans and coastal Kerala

s: Which one of the following statements regarding arid or desert soil is correct?
o: It is naturally rich in lime, humus and nitrogen
It is sandy, poor in nitrogen and humus, and improves with irrigation
It is waterlogged and rich in organic matter

3. Usar
4. Thur

s: The major causes of the formation of saline and alkaline soils include:

Accumulation of forest humus on mountain slopes

They are associated with waterlogged conditions

s: Which one of the following best describes forest and mountain soils?

Sandy soils rich in nitrogen and humus in western Rajasthan
Humus-rich soils on slopes, generally poor in potash and phosphorus
Salt-crusted soils of the coastal deltas

s: Which soil has the highest moisture-retention capacity among the soils listed?

Formation of deep trenches by concentrated surface flow

s:

s: Karewa soils are best described as:
o: Wind-deposited sandy soils of western Rajasthan
Lacustrine deposits forming plateaus above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley
Black cotton soils formed over basalt in the Deccan
Recent alluvial deposits of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta
x: Karewas are old lake-bed deposits of unconsolidated gravel and mud. They form plateau-like surfaces above the Jhelum plains in the Kashmir Valley and are also found in the Bhadarwah valley.
tq: Use the origin and landform description to identify the correct soil type.

s: Which one of the following statements about soil organic carbon is correct?

It reduces the water-holding capacity of clay soils in all conditions.
It disperses soil particles and reduces microbial activity.
